acquisition: Build exactly once through scripts/package-sdk.py; do not acquire MessagePack-CSharp or unity-sqlite-net separately through UPM.
install: Verify dependency-manifest.json and every recorded SHA-256 before copying.
Copy managed DLLs and their generated .meta files as one set; reference only the assemblies selected by the consumer asmdef plus their declared closure.
Copy only the native target subtree for the build host/target, retaining each adjacent generated and semantically validated target-isolated .meta file; upstream native importer metadata is not used.
Copy link.xml and retain the installed dependency-manifest.json as the ownership record.
upgrade: Verify the installed and replacement manifests.
Quiesce and close the application/database owner before replacing binaries.
Retain the complete previous bundle and consumer asmdef/import state, then replace only manifest-owned files atomically.
Never rewrite identities, cursors, immutable commands, migration journals, or player databases during a bundle upgrade.
uninstall: Quiesce and close the application/database owner.
Delete only paths listed by the installed dependency-manifest.json; do not delete saves, databases, pending commands, or consumer-owned .meta files.
Remove consumer precompiled references in the same coordinated change.

instructions: Quiesce the current owner and verify both current and retained previous manifests.
Restore the previous managed files and consumer references together; CL-013 contains no native or MessagePack qualification assembly.
Do not downgrade or delete databases; if the prior application cannot read the retained schema, leave rollback blocked and use forward recovery.

verificationPolicy.importable: sourceDirty must be false and build.buildSkipped must be false; ordinary --verify rejects any development artifact.
verificationPolicy.developmentInspection: --verify-development may inspect hashes and closure but prints DEVELOPMENT-ONLY and never makes the artifact importable or publishable.
verificationPolicy.nativeMetadata: Windows x86_64, macOS universal and Android ARM64 metadata is generated deterministically and checked semantically for exclusive platform, CPU, OS, exclusion and alignment settings.
